_doc: SHIFTZOOM: the Shift-constrained Ellipse drag run OFF the identity view.
draw_ellipse_shift.json runs at zoom 1.0, where the screen->document
conversion (`doc = (screen - view_offset) / zoom`, YamlTool's
pointer_event_payload in both ports) hands the tool exact integers, so
every doc-space anchor is a dyadic number and the arithmetic below is
exact by luck. That is why the original SHIFTCONSTRAIN smoke test — run
by hand at 100% zoom — saw a true circle.
At zoom 1.5 the anchor is NOT dyadic and the tool has to be right on
purpose. Geometry, by hand, from `doc = screen / 1.5` (offset 0):
press   screen ( 30,  50) -> doc ( 20, 100/3)
release screen (120,  95) -> doc ( 80, 190/3)
ddx = 80 - 20      = 60      (the furthest reach)
side = max(|ddx|, |ddy|) = 60      -> rx = ry = 30
The drag is down-and-right, so the shape grows into that quadrant from
the press point: the doc-space box is x 20..80, y 100/3..100/3+60, hence
cx = 50 and cy = 100/3 + 30 = 63.3333 (4 dp, the canonical rounding).
WHY THIS VECTOR NEEDS `expected_exact`. The canonical document JSON
rounds every float to 4 decimal places, so it CANNOT see the defect this
case exists for: before the fix the commit recovered the radius as
`abs(doc_end_y - doc_start_y) / 2`, re-subtracting the anchor that had
just been added to it, and 100/3 + 60 - 100/3 comes back one ulp heavy
(the sum crosses the 64 binade). rx was 30.0 and ry 30.000000000000004 —
an `ellipse`, not a circle — and the 4-dp golden below reads 30.0 either
way. The `expected_exact` block is the real gate: it compares the
committed doubles at FULL precision, exactly as `expected_view` does for
the view triple.
setup_svg is the same circle_basic.svg draw_ellipse_shift.json uses, so
the two vectors differ only in the view and the drag.
name: draw_ellipse_shift_zoomed_is_a_circle_at_non_dyadic_zoom
